learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to plan, conduct, and evaluate modeling and simulations (movements and stresses) for extensive mechanical assemblies and given questions.
Students know the types and functions of constraints and can apply them practically for modeling complex mechanical assemblies.
Students are able to create motion simulations for assemblies, interpret the results, and derive constructive changes.

Students can create models for stress analysis of mechanical assemblies and, considering the assumptions and simplifications made, evaluate the results and derive necessary constructive changes to optimize product design.
Independent task processing in teams conveys, in addition to specialized competencies, fundamental methodological competencies for practical product development.

syllabus_topics: Creation and linking of complex mechanical components using parametric modeling techniques and constraint modeling
Creation and handling of assemblies (Assembly techniques) considering variants and cross-component features
Creation, execution and evaluation of motion simulations, e.g., for function verification (kinematics) and collision control in manufacturing and assembly
Creation of models for FEM calculations of individual components including visualization and interpretation of simulation results
Initiation and cross-team coordination of changes
